msIdentifier.idno: MS MR.Frag.60.1 (fragment of the Iken Psalter)

provenance.orgName: Iken, Suffolk. Parish church of St Botulph
provenance.p: In 1987, the Supplement (p. 73) noted the following: Now split up. It appeared intact in a Sotheby sale, 10 December 1969, lot 36, and in Traylen's catalogue 77 (1972), no. 77, but one leaf appeared in Quaritch catalogue 1036 (1984), no. 16 and is now in private hands. In the aforementioned Quaritch catalogue, the following explanation is given for the provenance attribution: Possibly written for the church of St. Botulph at Iken in Suffolk. Botulph is one of only three English saints in the Litany and an inscription of Pond Hall and Orford on a flyleaf of the original manuscript indicates a Suffolk provenance.

The Iken Psalter and its dispersal is discussed in Eric J. Johnson and Scott Gwara, '"The Butcher's Bill: Using the Schoenberg Database to Reverse-Engineer Medieval and Renaissance Manuscript Books from Constituent Fragments', Manuscript Studies 1:2 (2016), pp. 250-52. Johnson and Gwara summarise that the manuscript was likely produced between 1290 and 1310; still existed in its medieval binding at the time of sale; originally consisted of seventy-six folios and included seven historiated initials, each itemized; included a “rough but impressive” full-page pen drawing of King Edmund the Martyr on a now missing flyleaf; contained a flyleaf inscription connecting it to Pond Hall and Orfforde in Suffolk; and was possibly written for the church of St. Botulph at Iken, also in Suffolk.
Johnson and Gwara identified several components, including the 9 folios now in Ohio State University. See also the Cornell University fragment, and the Cleveland Museum of Art fragment.
